newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks end firmer, helped by Wall St gains.
newsitem.headline: French stocks end firmer, helped by Wall St gains.

text.p: French shares closed higher, supported by a rising Wall Street, traders said. But trading in Paris suffered from low volume as London was closed for a market holiday.

The market earlier took heart from a BVA poll putting the centre-right coalition in a comfortable-but-reduced lead over the Socialists. Prime Minister Alain Juppe said he thought the election contest was getting closer.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed up 17.53 points or 0.66 percent at 2,672.84, while the CAC-40 futures contract was up 24 at 2,662 from Friday's close.
* Volume was a quiet 4.6 billion francs.
* Paribas, which went ex-dividend, gained 3.11 percent to 371.80.

* Thomson-CSF rose 2.33 percent to 184.20 francs, helped by newspaper reports Dasa of Germany was talking to rival bidders Lagardere and Alcatel Alsthom about possible cooperation after the privatisation. Lagardere was down 0.55 percent at 180, Alcatel was up 0.47 percent at 645.
* Active stocks with more than 200 million francs traded in each included Cie Generale des Eaux, down 1.35 percent at 806, and Axa, up 0.97 percent at 362.5.
* Accor denied market talk that it was looking to sell its Motel 6 chain. "It's the same old rumour from the same broker looking to push stock," said one trader. Accor ended up 2.81 percent at 879.
* Renault rises 3.43 percent to 141.7 francs, benefiting from French car sales figures last week which showed it outperforming the market.
A broker said the stock performed poorly last year and was due for a rise on its restructuring and on the positive effects seen from product launches.
* AGF continues catch-up, up 2.36 percent at 195.
* Sanofi gains 1.79 percent to 570, supported by continued market speculation of an industry consolidation.
* One broker said he thought the market could drift up to 2,700, on a view the centre-right coalition would regain power in the parliamentary election.

* A Louis Harris poll, published after the market close, showed the left gaining ground, with 45 percent of people polled wanting a Socialist/Communist win, against 43 percent wanting a conservative victory.
